title: Madison Dry Goods draws Halloween visitors with history, paranormal reports tied to 1929 tragedy

content:
A more-than-century-old building in downtown Madison that has served as a hardware store, hotel and funeral home is drawing new attention ahead of Halloween, blending local history with reports of paranormal activity.

The building, now home to Madison Dry Goods, was constructed in 1908 and later housed the TB Knight Funeral Home. It is also tied to one of the area’s most infamous tragedies. In 1929, the building became the site where the Lawson family was brought for viewing after a Christmas Day tragedy that claimed the lives of family members.

Today, an upstairs museum preserves the story of the Lawson family and the building’s connection to Madison’s past. The second floor includes the Lawson Family Murder Museum, which occupies the former embalming room where the victims of the 1929 Christmas Day massacre were prepared for burial.

Owner Jennifer Briggs said preserving that history is central to what the building represents.

“If it’s not preserved, then it’s just forgotten. And we really like to keep that history alive,” Briggs said.

At the same time, Briggs said the building’s past has fueled a reputation that draws visitors looking for something beyond artifacts and exhibits.

“It is very haunted,” she said. “We have, I’ve had people come in before, they’ll go upstairs and five minutes later they’re running out the front door.”

Briggs said visitors have reported strange sounds and unexplained encounters inside the building. She said she has experienced footsteps overhead and other unusual occurrences herself. Visitors have also reported hearing disembodied voices, seeing apparitions and feeling cold spots.

The museum includes historic rooms and artifacts from a time capsule that was buried in 1968 and opened 50 years later.

Briggs said she hopes visitors leave with an understanding that the building’s significance goes beyond ghost stories.

“I hope that they take away that this isn’t just a haunted building, that this is a piece of history,” she said.

Madison Dry Goods operates as a country store that doubles as a museum, offering visitors a nostalgic stop in the heart of downtown. The store is dog-friendly and offers outdoor seating. With paranormal investigations attracting curious visitors, the site continues to preserve the past while offering what Briggs described as a few spooky stories along the way.
